capabilities: Expose an allowlisted vault index to MCP clients via search, list, and fetch tools
Run an embedded local MCP server without an external Node installation
Enforce access levels (Off, scoped read, scoped read/write, GOD) for local file tools
Queue hosted write proposals for Obsidian-side diff review, approval, and apply
Time-box local filesystem access with a session window, user_intent gate, and JSONL audit trail
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; it is a public alpha installed via BRAT or manual release assets, with detailed setup and self-host docs in separate files (docs/self-host.md, docs/deployment.md, docs/local-server-mode.md). It includes extensive security disclosures, and local-only mode needs no accounts, telemetry, or paid service.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to give AI/MCP clients controlled access to vault context and files under user-defined allowlists, access levels, and audit rules.
